headline: The dashboard stopped losing its own cure
lede: A watch session older than three days was silently losing the very files it needed to resurrect dead panes — macOS wipes /tmp files untouched for that long at midnight. The supervisor now keeps its recipe permanently fresh, and a new nightly check proves a killed pane still comes back.

notes.text: #2278 shipped: the pane respawn recipe (baked scripts + panes.tsv) survives macOS tmp_cleaner — the supervisor touches its whole workspace every 5 s; touch moves atime+mtime and any inode change moves ctime, so the cleaner's three-stale-timestamps law can never catch a live session.

New gate npm run watchrespawncheck (CORE.checks): backdates a sandbox dashboard six days, demands every file revived two cycles later, runs the real cleaner predicate for zero matches, and replays #1259's kill-and-respawn end to end. Sandboxed; skips green off-mac.
The mutant run caught a weak pin: the source-check regex matched the commented-out fix. Pins are line-anchored now — a check that passes on its own mutation is blind.
ctime cannot be backdated, so same-day simulation can never prove death — the honest proof is a measured liveness invariant (backdate, then demand revival).
